headline: Spatial omics tools address transcript spillover and reliability of inferred expression
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Correction And Inference
summary: Dancer and SYNDRI target spillover in imaging spatial data, while RSC and REGAIN add noise and confidence awareness to histology-based expression inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is spatial transcriptomics, with methods addressing measurement artefacts and the reliability of predicted expression. In imaging-based platforms, Dancer uses a reference-guided probabilistic model to separate within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination. SYNDRI removes spillover after segmentation with a supervised transformer trained on simulated data. For histology-to-expression prediction, reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) splits RNA counts to benchmark against reproducible signal rather than noise, and REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence before TCGA-BRCA prognostic analysis. Other methods target spatial structure and composition. SCATTER deconvolves spots into cell-type proportions and per-cell-type profiles. GaLF-ST reconstructs expression with Gaussian latent fields. GLAND resolves small, non-contiguous domains, and GASTON-VI learns isodepth axes across samples and modalities. Spatial multi-omics fusion (SpatialMuSC, SPAMO) and cross-modal translation (scPriorDiff, scOnion) form a secondary thread. Bulk-to-single-cell work includes the generative Bulk2SC and closed-form accuracy bounds for deconvolution.
